correctness.rationale: The density establishes the exact valid parameter interval. For every integer m>=1 the centered rank-one kernel has the explicitly integrated eigenvalue alpha/[3(1+alpha)], and its lag-m total-variation coefficient equals B_m(s). The sign of its logarithmic derivative uniquely optimizes the positive branch; exact rational brackets prove the strictly better negative endpoint only for lag one and the strictly better positive branch for all later lags. An explicit limiting calculation proves the sharp asymptotic. The standalone supplied checker passed its exact symbolic and rational assertions; numerical grids were not used as proofs.

originality.rationale: The complete exact parameter-by-lag total-variation optimization, including the strict one-lag sign switch, the uniquely optimal positive parameter m+2sqrt(m) for every later lag, and the 2/(e m)3^{-(m-1)} envelope, is not contained in inspected sources. The rank-one composition technique and the exact copula-admissibility domain are prerequisites, not new stand-alone claims; literature priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: The absolute-regularity coefficient governs how a stationary copula Markov chain departs from independence in total variation. Optimizing this natural coefficient across the full valid model gives a precise unexpected sign switch after one lag, identifies unique lag-dependent optimal parameters, and reveals a 1/m correction to geometric worst-case decay. The additional total-variation/maximal-correlation discrepancy explains why standard spectral dependence alone misses finite-lag behavior.
